title: Lowest-row edge in a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $E_r^{p,q}$, $r\geq2$, be a cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] with $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\geq0$, and with differentials $d_r:E_r^{p,q}\to E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$. Suppose it abuts to objects $H^n$ equipped with finite decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration] $H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0$, together with the convergence identifications $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$, where $E_\infty=Z_\infty/B_\infty$ is formed from the pages and differentials by the recursive cycle and boundary subobjects of $E_2$ of [def-sp-convergence] (in this first-quadrant situation each $Z_r^{p,q}$ and $B_r^{p,q}$ is constant for $r>\max(p,q+1)$). Let $m\geq0$, and suppose $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for every $p\geq0$ and $0\leq q<m$. Then $E_2^{0,m}$ survives canonically to $E_\infty^{0,m}$, $F^1H^m=0$, and the canonical left edge $H^m\to E_2^{0,m}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 011O, definition-limit-spectral-sequence (degeneration and stable pages); Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss (finite abutment filtrations). Agent-extracted lowest-row consequence of these notions; no assertion that either tag states this precise edge criterion.

proof.text: For each natural r, propagate the vanishing of entries with p<0 or q<m from page 2 to page r+2. At page 2, negative coordinates use hfirst; otherwise write p and q as natural numbers and apply hrow. At a successor use ShortComplex.isZero_homology_of_isZero_X₂ and E.iso. This proves precisely the page vanishings needed below.

source.place: Tag 011N, definition-spectral-sequence: successor page is homology; elementary induction from the hypotheses.

proof.text: At (0,m), on page r+2 the outgoing target is (r+2,m-(r+2)+1), whose second coordinate is less than m; the incoming source is (-(r+2),m+(r+2)-1), whose first coordinate is negative. Step 1 makes both differentials zero. Compute the next and previous indices of the complex shape explicitly. Mathlib HomologicalComplex.iCyclesIso and isoHomologyπ then identify the entry with its cycles and its homology by the canonical inclusion and projection. Let s r be the composite of the inverse cycle inclusion, homology projection and E.iso. Define a 0 as the identity and a (r+1) as a r followed by s r, and define b r as (a r).hom followed by the inverse cycle inclusion. The recursion and the canonical isomorphism equations give both required compatibility identities. This implements the stationary cycle/boundary comparison directly on the pages of [def-sp-spectral-sequence].

source.place: Tag 011O, definition-limit-spectral-sequence and preceding recursive cycle/boundary construction; elementary bidegree calculation.

proof.text: For 1≤p≤m, Step 1 makes the page m+2 entry (p,m-p) zero, because m-p<m. Transport this zero object through the supplied convergence isomorphism conv m p (m-p). By [def-sp-filtration], this is exactly the cokernel defining the graded piece (F m).gr p.

source.place: Tag 011O, definition-limit-spectral-sequence; Tag 0121, definition-filtered. The graded-piece identifications are hypotheses, not an invocation of the double-complex theorem 0132.

proof.text: For 1≤p≤m, the inclusion F^(p+1)→F^p is monic. Its cokernel is zero by Step 3, so Preadditive.epi_of_isZero_cokernel makes it epic. Since the category is abelian [def-sp-abelian], it is an isomorphism, hence the two subobjects are equal by Subobject.eq_of_comm. Induct on k≤m starting at F^(m+1)=0 to obtain F^(m+1-k)=0. Taking k=m gives F^1=0. The same induction covers m=0 using only the terminal hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0121, definition-filtered; elementary finite-filtration argument from the normal-monomorphism axiom, written out here.

proof.text: Put f=Subobject.ofLE(F^1≤F^0). Since F^1=0 by Step 4, its arrow into H m is zero; cancellation against the monic arrow of F^0 shows f=0. Thus cokernel.π f is an isomorphism by cokernel.π_of_zero. The arrow F^0→H m is an isomorphism because F^0=top. Define edge as the inverse of that arrow, followed by cokernel.π f, followed by the supplied conv m 0 m, followed by the inverse of a m from Step 2. Every factor is an isomorphism. Cancelling the inverse pairs proves exactly the displayed quotient square, hence gives the asserted canonical edge and IsIso edge.

source.place: Tag 011O, definition-limit-spectral-sequence; Tag 0121, definition-filtered; explicit edge-map composite from the assumed convergence data.

proof_origin.place: Elementary lowest-row consequence of Tags 011N, 011O and 0121, with the finite abutment filtration and its comparisons assumed. S4 implements canonical survival directly using Mathlib iCyclesIso and isoHomologyπ, finite reverse induction on the filtration, and the explicit quotient-square edge composite; the exact-couple convergence API is not needed.

lean.statement: theorem first_quadrant_lowest_row_edge {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (E : E₂CohomologicalSpectralSequence C) (hfirst : ∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 ∨ q < 0 → IsZero ((E.page 2).X (p, q))) (H : ℕ → C) (F : ∀ n : ℕ, DecreasingFiltration (H n)) (htop : ∀ n : ℕ, (F n).F 0 = ⊤) (hbottom : ∀ n : ℕ, (F n).F ((n : ℤ) + 1) = ⊥) (conv : ∀ (n p q : ℕ) (_hpq : p + q = n), (F n).gr p ≅ (E.page ((n : ℤ) + 2)).X (p, q)) (m : ℕ) (hrow : ∀ p q : ℕ, q < m → IsZero ((E.page 2).X (p, q))) : ∃ (a : ∀ r : ℕ, (E.page 2).X (0, m) ≅ (E.page ((r : ℤ) + 2)).X (0, m)) (b : ∀ r : ℕ, (E.page 2).X (0, m) ⟶ (E.page ((r : ℤ) + 2)).cycles (0, m)), (a 0).hom = 𝟙 _ ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, b r ≫ (E.page ((r : ℤ) + 2)).iCycles (0, m) = (a r).hom ∧ b r ≫ (E.page ((r : ℤ) + 2)).homologyπ (0, m) ≫ (E.iso ((r : ℤ) + 2) ((r : ℤ) + 3) (0, m)).hom = (a (r + 1)).hom) ∧ (F m).F 1 = ⊥ ∧ ∃ edge : H m ⟶ (E.page 2).X (0, m), ((F m).F 0).arrow ≫ edge ≫ (a m).hom = cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ ((F m).F_succ_le 0)) ≫ (conv m 0 m (by omega)).hom ∧ IsIso edge
lean.note: The recursive E-infinity subquotient is represented by its canonically identified stationary page n+2 in total degree n. The cycles/homology recursion specifies survival on every page; the quotient square specifies the canonical left edge. No exact-couple hypothesis is imposed.
